questions.question: Why is the six membered cyclic structure of glucose called a pyranose structure?

options.text: Furan is a five membered cyclic compound, with one oxygen and four carbon atoms.
Pyran is a non-cyclic organic compound, with one oxygen atom and five carbon atoms in the ring.
Furan is a five membered non-cyclic compound, with one oxygen and four carbon atoms.
Pyran is a cyclic organic compound, with one oxygen atom and five carbon atoms in the ring.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** ​Pyran is a cyclic organic compound, with one oxygen atom and five carbon atoms in the ring.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The six-membered cyclic structure of glucose is called a **pyranose **because it resembles the structure of a chemical compound called **pyran**.
 
• Pyran is a **six-membered ring with five carbon atoms and one oxygen atom.**
 
• In glucose, the six-membered ring forms when the hydroxyl group (-OH) on carbon 5 reacts with the aldehyde group (C=O) on carbon 1, creating a **hemiacetal linkage.**
 
• This reaction forms a ring that includes one oxygen atom and five carbon atoms, just like pyran. Hence, the glucose ring structure is termed a pyranose ring.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• Glucose, as a carbohydrate, is a fundamental biomolecule involved in various biological processes.
 
• The** pyranose structure of glucose represents its cyclic form**, which is crucial in biochemistry for understanding how glucose behaves in cells, participates in metabolism, and forms larger polysaccharides like starch and cellulose.

questions.question: In which of the following regions of India is the Mundari language spoken?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chota - Nagpur plateau.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Chota Nagpur Plateau is a rich cultural and geographical region in eastern India, covering parts of **Jharkhand, Odisha, West Bengal, and Bihar.**
 
• It is home to several indigenous tribal communities, including the** Munda people**, who are the primary speakers of the Mundari language. 
 
• The Munda people, along with other indigenous tribes like the Santals and Oraons, have traditionally inhabited the Chota Nagpur Plateau. 
 
• The Chota Nagpur Plateau is known for its vast forests, rich mineral deposits, and hilly terrain.
 
• It includes major districts such as **Ranchi, Gumla, Khunti** (in Jharkhand), and parts of northern **Odisha and West Bengal.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Malwa Plateau** in central India (mostly Madhya Pradesh) is predominantly inhabited by** Hindi and Malvi **speakers.
 
• The **Thar Desert **is in western India, covering Rajasthan and parts of Gujarat, where** Rajasthani and Marwari **are the common languages.
 
• **Baghelkhand** is a region in northeastern Madhya Pradesh, known for dialects of **Hindi and Bagheli.**

questions.question: A school teacher asks students to stand up every time national anthem is sung. Which Article enshrines this fundamental duty?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 51 (a).**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The fundamental duty to respect the national anthem is enshrined in **Article 51A(a) **of the Indian Constitution.
 
• This article is part of the Fundamental Duties listed in Part IVA, which were added by the **42nd Amendment Act, 1976.**
 
• Article 51A(a) states that it is the duty of every citizen of India:
 
 
• "To abide by the Constitution and respect its ideals and institutions, the National Flag and the National Anthem."
 
 
 
• In addition to being enshrined in Article 51A(a) of the Constitution, the obligation to respect the National Anthem is also reinforced by the Supreme Court of India. In its 2005 ruling in the** Bijoe Emmanuel vs. State of Kerala case.**
 
• The **Prevention of Insults to National Honour Act, 1971** also provides guidelines on respecting the National Anthem and Flag. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** All the Fundamental Duties as per Article 51A of the Indian Constitution, which was added by the** 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976:**

 
 

 Article
 Fundamental Duty
 
 
 
 

 51A(a)
 To abide by the Constitution and respect its ideals and institutions, the National Flag, and the National Anthem.
 
 

 51A(b)
 To cherish and follow the noble ideals which inspired our national struggle for freedom.
 
 

 51A(c)
 To uphold and protect the sovereignty, unity, and integrity of India.
 
 

 51A(d)
 To defend the country and render national service when called upon to do so.
 
 

 51A(e)
 To promote harmony and the spirit of common brotherhood amongst all the people of India, transcending religious, linguistic, and regional or sectional diversities; to renounce practices derogatory to the dignity of women.
 
 

 51A(f)
 To value and preserve the rich heritage of our composite culture.
 
 

 51A(g)
 To protect and improve the natural environment, including forests, lakes, rivers, wildlife, and to have compassion for living creatures.
 
 

 51A(h)
 To develop the scientific temper, humanism, and the spirit of inquiry and reform.
 
 

 51A(i)
 To safeguard public property and to abjure violence.
 
 

 51A(j)
 To strive towards excellence in all spheres of individual and collective activity, so that the nation constantly rises to higher levels of endeavor and achievement.
 
 

 51A(k)
 To provide opportunities for education to children between the ages of 6 and 14 years and ensure that they receive this education (added by the 86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002).
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **__Important Points__****Article 51**

**Promotion of international peace and security:**

 
• The State shall—
 
 
• (a) promote international peace and security;
 
• (b) maintain just and honorable relations between nations;
 
• (c) foster respect for international law and treaty obligations in the dealings of organized peoples with one another; and
 
• (d) encourage settlement of international disputes by arbitration.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements is/are true with respect to MRTP Act?

i) The Monopolies and Restrictive Trade Practices Act (MRTP Act) was repealed and replaced by the Competition Act, 2002.

ii) The asset limit for MRTP companies was fixed at Rs. 25 crores by the first/original Monopolies and Restrictive Trade Practices Act (MRTP Act).

iii) The Monopolies and Restrictive Trade Practices Act (MRTP Act) was first passed in 1969.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only i and iii**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• i) **True**: The MRTP Act was indeed repealed and replaced by the Competition Act, 2002, which aimed to promote and sustain competition in the markets.
 
• ii) **False**: The original asset limit for MRTP companies **was set at Rs. 20 crores, not Rs. 25 crores.**
 
• iii)**True**: The MRTP Act was enacted in 1969 to prevent monopolistic and restrictive trade practices.
 
• Thus, **statements i and iii are true** with respect to the MRTP Act.

questions.question: Which type of electromagnetic radiation was discovered by Johann Wilhelm Ritter in 1801?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Ultraviolet rays.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Johann Wilhelm Ritter discovered ultraviolet (UV) radiation in 1801.
 
• He identified it while experimenting with silver chloride and observing that it darkened when exposed to light beyond the violet end of the visible spectrum.
 
• This marked the first discovery of electromagnetic radiation beyond the visible spectrum. 
 
• Types of UV Rays: UV radiation is categorized into three types based on wavelength:
 
 
• UVA (320-400 nm): These rays penetrate the skin more deeply and are associated with skin aging and long-term skin damage.
 
• UVB (290-320 nm): These rays are primarily responsible for sunburn and play a significant role in developing skin cancer.
 
• UVC (100-290 nm): These rays are the most harmful but are mostly absorbed by the Earth's ozone layer and do not reach the surface.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__

questions.question: Which cost is considered for calculating the national income in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Factor cost.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• This refers to the cost of production factors (land, labor, capital, and entrepreneurship) used to produce goods and services, excluding indirect taxes and including subsidies.
 
• National income is often calculated at factor cost** to reflect the income earned by factors of production**, giving a more accurate measure of economic performance.
 
• It reflects the income earned by factors of production and provides a** clear view of the economy's performance. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Product Cost**:

 
 
• This encompasses all costs associated with** the production of goods**, including direct materials, direct labor, and manufacturing overhead.
 
• While product cost can influence pricing and profit calculations, it is not directly used to calculate national income in the same way as factor cost.
 
 
 
• **Market Cost**:
 
 
• This is the price at which goods and services are sold in the market, **including taxes and excluding subsidies.**
 
• National income can be expressed in terms of market prices, but adjustments for taxes and subsidies are necessary to derive factor cost for a more accurate measure.
 
 
 
• **Sunk Cost**:
 
 
• This refers to costs that have already been incurred and **cannot be recovered.** Sunk costs should not influence future economic decisions.
 
• Sunk costs are not relevant for calculating national income, as they do not reflect current production or income generation.

questions.question: Who founded a reformist organisation called ‘Brahmo Samaj’ in Calcutta?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Raja Ram Mohan Roy**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Raja Ram Mohan Roy was born on **May 22, 1772, in Radhanagar, Hooghly District, Bengal**
 
• The Brahmo Samaj was **founded in 1828** by Raja Ram Mohan Roy in Calcutta (now Kolkata).
 
• The Brahmo Samaj advocates belief in a **Monotheism, "Infinite Singularity"** that is infinite, indivisible, imperceptible, and indefinable.
 
• It promoted women's education and upliftment,** abolition of **social practices such as **Sati, child marriage, and the caste system.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar** was born on September 26, 1820, in Birsingha village, West Bengal.
 
• Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar was a staunch** advocate for gender equality and the upliftment of women in society**.
 
• **Vinoba Bhave** was born on September 11, 1895, in Gagode village, Raigad, Maharashtra.
 
• In 1951, Vinoba Bhave started the **Bhoodan (land gift) movement**,
 
• He was awarded the** Ramon Magsaysay Award** for Community Leadership in 1958.

• Maḥmūd was the** first to carry the banner of Islam** into the heart of India.

• **Library of Alexandria** Became a center of learning and culture in the **Hellenistic world**.

questions.question: Western disturbances are responsible for:

options.text: extremely chilled weather of north-east India
dusty storms in eastern costal area of India
hot winds during summers in northern India
rainfall during winters in north-western part of India

questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** rainfall during winters in north-western part of India**__.

__
 
• Western Disturbances are extratropical storms originating in the Mediterranean region.
 
• They travel eastwards, affecting the weather patterns across Northern India, Pakistan, Nepal, and even extending to Bangladesh.
 
• Western Disturbances bring sudden winter rains to the plains and snow to the mountains of the northwestern Indian subcontinent.
 
• These disturbances are vital for the cultivation of Rabi crops.

questions.question: Which of the following is an input device?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Keyboard**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

• **Keyboard:**

 
 
• **Primary Input Device:** Used to enter text, numbers, and commands into a computer.
 
• Includes mechanical, membrane, and virtual keyboards.
 
• QWERTY, AZERTY, and Dvorak layouts.
 
• **Shortcut Keys:**
 
 
• Ctrl + C: Copy
 
• Ctrl + V: Paste
 
• Ctrl + X: Cut
 
• Ctrl + Z: Undo
 
• Ctrl + S: Save
 
• Alt + Tab: Switch between open applications
 
• Ctrl + F: Find
 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Monitor:**

 
 
• It is an **output device** that displays information in visual form.
 
• Commonly known as a screen or display.
 
 
 
• **Printer:**
 
 
• It is an** output device **that produces a** hard copy of digital documents**.
 
• Converts digital data into printed material.
 
• Types include inkjet, laser, and dot matrix printers.
 
 
 
• **Speaker:**
 
 
• It is an** output device **that produces sound.
 
• Converts digital audio signals into audible sound.
